title: Advanced connectors and cohesion
grammar: Advanced connectors (despite, due to, so as to)

sections.heading: Connectors review
sections.body: At B1 you learned basic connectors (however, although, because, so). At B2 we expand the range with more formal and nuanced connectors for writing and speaking.

sections.heading: Contrast connectors
table: Although he was tired, he finished.
Despite the rain, we went out.
I like coffee, whereas she prefers tea.
I don't hate it. On the contrary, I love it.
It was expensive. Nevertheless, I bought it.

sections.heading: Cause and reason
table: Since it was late, we left.
We left because of the noise.
The delay was due to the weather.
Owing to the strike, buses are cancelled.
On account of the rain, we cancelled.

sections.heading: Purpose connectors
table: I left early to catch the train.
She studies in order to improve.
He left early so as to avoid traffic.
I left early so that I wouldn't be late.
I went to the shop for bread.

sections.heading: Consequence connectors
table: It rained, so we stayed home.
The road was closed; therefore, we detoured.
He studied hard. As a result, he passed.
She missed the bus; consequently, she was late.
The project failed; thus, we need a new plan.

sections.heading: Adding and clarifying
list: Moreover / Furthermore: formal addition. The plan is expensive. Moreover, it is risky.
In addition: In addition, we offer free delivery.
Besides: Besides being cheap, it is also fast.
In other words: In other words, we need to start again.
That is to say: That is to say, the situation is critical.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not use 'although' with a noun: use 'despite' or 'in spite of'.
Do not confuse 'due to' (cause) with 'in order to' (purpose).
'However' is followed by a comma and a new sentence.

phases.name: Discovery
phases.intro: Look at these sentences. Read them carefully and think about the questions below.
sentences: Although he was tired, he finished the race.
Despite the rain, we went for a walk.
Since it was late, we decided to leave.
The delay was due to the weather.
She studies in order to improve her English.
He left early so as to avoid the traffic.
The road was closed; therefore, we took another route.
The plan is expensive. Moreover, it is risky.
questions: In sentences 3 and 4, what is the difference between 'since' and 'due to'?
In sentences 5 and 6, what do 'in order to' and 'so as to' express?
In sentence 8, what is the role of 'moreover'?

questions.prompt: ___ the bad weather, the event was a success.
The delay was ___ to technical problems.
questions.explanation: Due to is a formal way to express cause.

questions.prompt: She studied hard ___ pass the exam.
It was raining. ___ , we decided to stay home.
___ he was tired, he continued working.
I like tea, ___ she prefers coffee.
questions.explanation: Whereas introduces a comparison or contrast.

questions.prompt: He left early ___ avoid the traffic.
The project failed. ___ , we need a new plan.
___ the strike, buses are cancelled.
The hotel was expensive. ___ , the service was poor.

phases.name: Free practice
prompts: Write a short argumentative paragraph (6-8 sentences) using at least 4 formal connectors.
Rewrite 5 sentences using more formal connectors: 'because' → 'due to', 'but' → 'however', 'so' → 'therefore'.
Write a formal essay paragraph about the environment using 'despite', 'due to', 'in order to', 'moreover'.

questions.prompt: ___ the rain, we went to the beach.
The flight was cancelled ___ the storm.
She left early ___ miss the train.
questions.explanation: So as not to + verb for negative purpose.

questions.prompt: It was very cold. ___ , we went skiing.
___ he studied hard, he didn't pass.
I love chocolate, ___ my brother hates it.
questions.explanation: Whereas introduces contrast between two facts.

questions.prompt: He stayed home ___ his illness.
The results were excellent. ___ , the team celebrated.
___ the traffic, we arrived on time.
The plan is expensive. ___ , it is risky.

sections.heading: Key rules
list: Contrast: although + clause; despite / in spite of + noun.
Cause: because / since / as + clause; due to / owing to + noun.
Purpose: in order to / so as to + verb; so that + clause.
Consequence: so (informal); therefore / consequently / thus (formal).
Addition: moreover / furthermore / in addition.
'However' is followed by a comma and a new sentence.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not use 'although' with a noun; use 'despite'.
Do not confuse 'due to' (cause) with 'in order to' (purpose).
'However' does not join two clauses with a comma only.

sections.heading: Useful phrases
list: Despite the..., ...
Due to the..., ...
In order to..., I...
...; therefore, ...
...; consequently, ...
Moreover, ...
As a result, ...
